newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset says reports "in line" with results.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset says reports "in line" with results.

text.p: Italian broadcaster Mediaset said data published in two Italian newspapers on Wednesday regarding its expected results for 1996 "are in line with what will be discussed tomorrow by the board."

Financial dailies Il Sole 24 Ore and Milano Finanza earlier reported Mediaset was expected to show a consolidated net profit of 445-450 billion lire for 1996, a fraction lower than 454.6 billion in 1995.
The newspapers said Mediaset's board was considering raising the dividend for 1996, which in 1995 was 175 lire per share.
Mediaset said in a statement: "As far as the dividend is concerned, the relevant proposal will be examined and then formulated during the board meeting."
It intended to issue a statement after Thursday's board meeting, it said.

The papers said parent profits at Mediaset, which is controlled by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest group, were 371 billion, up 128 billion on 1995, while total consolidated turnover reached 3.1 to 3.2 trillion lire in 1996 from 2.925 trillion in 1995.
They said in 1994 and 1995 Mediaset benefited from tax breaks under the Tremonti law, paying respectively 21.4 percent and 40.6 percent in taxes. The tax benefits were no longer available in 1996.
